newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 18.

text.p: Two executives at Archer Daniels Midland Co who are being investigated by federal regulators for price fixing have stepped down from their posts. Shareholders nearly approved a measure on board independence, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
- The Canadian Automobile Workers union wants General Motors Co to maintain pay and benefits for its workers even if it sells two parts plants in Canada.
- U.S. ports are going through major changes that are shifting tens of thousands of jobs and billions of dollars of cargo among coastal towns.

- Companies are racing to find a new drug to fight Hepatitis C after biotechnology companies Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc and Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc identified the structure of a protein crucial to the disease's reproduction.
- Mexican grocery stores Controladora Comercial Mexicana issued global depositary shares even though the country's consumers have no money and their wages are not keeping up with inflation.
- British publisher Pearson Plc appointed Marjorie Scardino as chief executive officer.
- A Morgan Stanley Group Inc bond trader took a $25 million loss in July, one of the firm's biggest losses on a single position.
- Fidelity Export Fund had great returns even though some investors took out their money earlier this year.
- AT&T Corp saw its profits from continuing operations fall 11 percent during the last quarter.
- Bell Atlantic Corp, BellSouth Corp, Pacific Telesis Group and SBC Communications Inc reported robust quarterly profits.
- Bankers Trust New York Corp's quarterly profit climbed 14 percent, KeyCorp reported a flat performance and Bank of Boston Corp had a 54-percent fall.
- Allstate Corp 's income from continuing operations were higher than expected.
- In September, U.S. home building fell 6.0 percent and industrial output edged 0.2 percent higher.
- The Dow Jones industrial average ended higher at 6,059.20, the second record in a row, while bond prices moved higher on inflation figures and the U.S. dollar closed mixed.
- U.S. indicators showing the country's economy growing slower encouraged bond traders to push the 30-year Treasury bond to its highest level in more than a week.
